title: Greedy Routing in a Sequentially Grown One-Dimensional Random Graph
summary: We analyze greedy routing in a random graph G_n constructed on the vertex set V = {1, 2, ..., n} embedded in Z. Vertices are inserted according to a uniform random permutation pi, and each newly inserted vertex connects to its nearest already-inserted neighbors on the left and right (if they exist). This work addresses a conjecture originating from empirical studies (Ponomarenko et al., 2011; Malkov et al., 2012), which observed through simulations that greedy search in sequentially grown graphs exhibits logarithmic routing complexity across various dimensions.
